title: MMSU Gold mango (NSIC Mn 01): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: MMSU Gold mango: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: MMSU Gold mango is a Carabao mango variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: MMSU Gold mango is a Carabao mango variety, also sold or known as NSIC Mn 01. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1997 as NSIC 1997 Mn 01. MMSU bred it. Its record notes a yield of 490 kg.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where MMSU Gold mango is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Mn 01, this is the same mango. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [mango variety finder](/crop-varieties/mango), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).
Key facts about MMSU Gold mango
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of MMSU Gold was about 50 years old and about 35 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 490 kg. It bears regularly, with fruit in March May. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit mango fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Mango cecid fly (kurikong)](/pests/mango-cecid-fly), [Mango leafhopper](/pests/mango-leafhopper), [Mango pulp weevil](/pests/mango-pulp-weevil), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of MMSU Gold weighs about 288 grams, and its shape is oblong. The flesh is yellow and smooth and firm. Its sweetness measured 18 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 74.31 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is March May, bearing regular.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Harvest:** Fruits March to May, regular bearer.
**Fruit:** About 288 g, yellow orange peel, smooth, firm, fiberless yellow flesh, 18 Brix.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the first NSIC numbered mango, an Ilocos Carabao strain that bears every year. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant MMSU Gold mango

The Carabao mango is the one the market wants, and the registered strains are its best trees, picked for size, sweetness and steady bearing. Buy grafted seedlings from a BPI accredited nursery so you get the strain you paid for. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is NSIC Mn 01 the same as MMSU Gold?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Mn 01 is another name for MMSU Gold, registered as NSIC 1997 Mn 01. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 490 kg. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of MMSU Gold?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
